reviews.text:
I previously used this clinic's services, but the service was sloppy, and there was even a surgical error.

I used their services for both dogs and cats. When I sought a second opinion at another clinic, they carefully considered the treatment plan based on scientific data. However, this clinic sometimes relied on past experience, which, while important, increased my anxiety and distrust when entrusting the lives of my beloved family members to them. Unfortunately, I switched to another clinic.

The other clinic conducted multiple tests, performed detailed diagnoses, and found the optimal treatment plan. Most importantly, I regret having to accept the lingering after-effects of the surgery without recourse.

Not all of my experience was bad, so I hesitated to post this, but I wanted to share this information so others don't have to go through the same thing.

There were times when I had to be overly cautious when deciding on a treatment plan, suggesting there may be issues with their communication skills.

This is my first review, so I apologize if it's difficult to read.

I visited because my cat was unwell.

I have multiple cats, and I had previously left my mother cat at their pet hotel, but it had been several years since my last visit for a check-up. Honestly, I wish I had come sooner.

Whenever I go to the vet, I'm always filled with anxiety and tension, wondering what if it's a serious illness.

The vet I used to go to had a somewhat tense atmosphere from the reception, which always made me nervous. This vet, however, had a surprisingly warm and welcoming atmosphere from the moment I opened the door.

The receptionist was very kind, which helped me relax a little.

While filling out the questionnaire, I could faintly hear the doctor talking to other patients, and the atmosphere was very peaceful, which was reassuring.

During the examination, the doctor listened carefully to my concerns about my cat's condition and daily life, at my own pace, allowing me to speak calmly.

Furthermore, they explained the current situation and future treatment plan very carefully, in a way that even a layperson could understand.

The doctor even shared stories about their own cat, which made me chuckle at times.

I think it was the first time I'd ever laughed at a veterinary clinic.

They asked, "Is there anything else you're concerned about? Please tell me anything, and I'll answer all your questions," and by then, my tension had completely melted away, and I was able to discuss everything in a relaxed manner.

After the examination, the way they treated the person with a dog who came in after me was also very warm, and seeing that, I naturally decided that I wanted to entrust my pet's care to this clinic in the future.

When I left, the doctor and reception staff kindly saw me off, and I headed home feeling positive.

I think the hospital I had been going to before was also wonderful.

However, this experience strongly reinforced my belief that the atmosphere of the hospital and compatibility with the doctor are truly important.

I would like to entrust the care of my beloved family member to this clinic in the future.

Please excuse my rambling.

I stopped going to this vet because the male doctor's overbearing attitude and the incompatible communication were too stressful. It even made me feel unwell. Also, the explanations about medication were vague, like "It's okay to give them all together." A second opinion revealed that the medication was too strong for my elderly dog. Previously, my dog ​​had often gotten sick from medications that didn't agree with him. The male doctor's mood was very inconsistent, and I was always nervous. There are many other veterinary clinics nearby that are more polite, normal, and competent. An acquaintance left their cat there, and when they went back the next morning, it had already died. They were charged 80,000 yen for a procedure performed without consultation. They regretted that they hadn't received any contact after dropping off their cat the day before, wondering if it had been left unattended overnight.


While some people have given high ratings, I wonder if they were just lucky enough to visit when the male doctor was in a good mood?

This was my first visit.
First of all, I was amazed that they waited until my cat was relaxed before the examination!
They also explained in detail that ultrasound can potentially detect problems earlier than blood tests, and even showed me the ultrasound images, which was very informative and reassuring!

The doctor pointed out my shortcomings as a pet owner and also patiently addressed even my smallest concerns.
I was also surprised to learn that the doctor tests the effects of various treatments on their own body before testing them on animals.
Thank you especially for teaching me so much about the intestines!

In the case of typical watery diarrhea, the going rate around Waseda is less than 30,000 yen, but I was suddenly billed 60,000 yen without any explanation of the treatment or progress report.

Upon seeking a second opinion, I discovered that unnecessary tests had been performed.

I left my dog ​​at this veterinary clinic while I was away on a business trip, and they treated his diarrhea. While I was grateful for the treatment itself, there was absolutely no prior explanation about my dog's condition, the treatment plan, or the costs. When I went to pick him up, I was suddenly presented with an additional bill of 60,000 yen, which was a huge shock.

For humans, informed consent is essential, and explanations of treatment plans and costs are a given. I believe the same should apply to pets; owners should have the opportunity to make informed decisions. However, this hospital didn't explain the options or costs before treatment, and the sudden, high bill after treatment left me with a strong sense of distrust.

If they had shared information about my dog's symptoms and treatment plan beforehand, I could have researched it and made an informed decision about whether or not to proceed. I believe trust is paramount in a veterinary clinic, and it's disappointing that this was lacking.

I felt that this hospital prioritized money over the feelings and trust of pet owners. I will never use their services again, and I strongly advise anyone who doesn't want to experience the same thing to be very careful.
I was so worried when my dad got sick, but the doctor was so kind and cured his serious illness. Thank you so much.
I was full of worries about owning a rabbit for the first time, but they kindly answered all my questions. I felt reassured knowing that I could come back here if anything happened!

I'm going to this hospital because a foreign friend recommended it to me. Japanese is not my native language, but the doctor understands it and always explains things to me carefully and kindly.
My beloved cat had her spayed/neutered in the morning and I couldn't take her home until the next day, but the doctor sensed my anxiety and allowed me to come and see my cat in the evening after the surgery.
I think the doctor is very kind!

My friend, who doesn't speak Japanese, also used this veterinarian and said that he was wonderful. He doesn't speak English, but does his best. He also helped them out with all the documentation and procedures required for moving abroad with your pets and told me he'd be happy to help me if I ever needed to move abroad with my cat too!

I took my cat to the vet when she became ill.

Her condition didn't improve, so I had tests done. During the tests, my cat was taken to a back room, and I was shown a paper with the test results written by the vet, who diagnosed her with "anemia."

I was pressured into expensive treatments, injections, and IV fluids. The vet was condescending and made completely irrelevant comments, such as asking if I didn't love my cat. I also felt distrustful of the vet, who was always absent from the clinic when no one was there. The next day, I went to a different hospital for a re-examination.

As expected, the vet at the other animal hospital told me that "there were no signs of anemia, so the treatment would be pointless." Worried about my cat, I also went to a university hospital for a thorough examination, but they also stated that "there were no abnormalities, and the levels were not indicative of anemia."

Thinking about how my cat would have suffered due to a misdiagnosis if I had continued going to that hospital, I truly realized the importance of seeking a second opinion.
Took my cat there and the doctor was patient with me for being the first time cat owner. Was a nice experience overall
